status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: Privacy and individual autonomy are relevant to the alleged processing of a non-user’s meeting contribution. The complaint alleges recording and voiceprint derivation without consent. Voluntary dismissal did not resolve those allegations. Cruz-specific meeting permissions and a forensic voice template are not available. Other plaintiffs’ cases do not supply those facts.

conclusion_change.previous: The complaint describes two processing steps affecting a non-user participant: recording and transcription, then alleged biometric derivation from her speech. The suit’s voluntary dismissal without prejudice did not resolve either occurrence. Later cases involving other plaintiffs and Fireflies’ general policy do not establish Cruz’s meeting-level permissions or whether a voiceprint was generated. Both findings remain unresolved. Participant recording and alleged voiceprint derivation remain separate unresolved steps. Voluntary dismissal without prejudice resolves neither event, and other plaintiffs’ proceedings do not supply Cruz-specific permissions or a forensic biometric template. No admitted local or independently source-identified canonical requirement is established.
